thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Sev2 - Repeated OOMs + container crashes observed on inference-runtime in us-west-2. Spike started ~2024-11-02T02:15Z. Multiple pods restarted; autoscale triggered but churn persists. Please triage.

maria: ack @incident-bot, I'm on it. grabbing logs and starting heap dump collection.

ajay: seeing lots of `CUDA out of memory` traces from allocator (kb-allocator) on pid 4213. stack shows paged-attention allocations failing after long sessions.

simon: metrics show steady resident growth of kv_cache on many workers — looks like slow leak/fragmentation rather than sudden blowup. frag_ratio creeping up over hours.

tess: @infra-bot can you check for node-level GPU driver resets? that would explain the container crashes.

infra-bot: Noted. nodes i-0abc12345 and i-0def67890 showing GPU resets and kernel logs indicating driver reconnections. Scheduling cordon/drain for those nodes now.

maria: quick customer note — small set of customers reported 502s/timeouts. Not a global outage but visible. CCing @customer-ops.

customer-ops: acknowledged. compiling impacted customer list and opening support threads for any with P0 symptoms.

ajay: kicked off heap dump collector on 2 affected pods, command:
```
kubectl exec -it inference-pod-4213 -- /opt/runtime/collect_heap --out /tmp/heap-4213.tgz
kubectl exec -it inference-pod-4227 -- /opt/runtime/collect_heap --out /tmp/heap-4227.tgz
```

simon: enabling debug kv metrics (kv.cache.frag_ratio, kv.cache.evictions) and bumping eviction frequency temporarily. Also enabling verbose allocator logging for a short window.

tess: can we route a small percent to a fallback model variant with smaller KV footprint to see if that reduces error rate?

maria: creating canary route to model-2-quant-fast (smaller KV usage), 5% split. running now.

incident-bot: Deploy event: canary -> model-2-quant-fast at 7169876600 by maria

ajay: after canary rollout, error rate on canary instances dropped ~80%. non-canary still elevated. good signal.

simon: grep of heap dump shows repeated lines like `kv_block: freed but not coalesced` and many small free fragments. suggests slab fragmentation — small allocations never merged back.

maria: ordering node drains for worst nodes and rescheduling pods to fresh hosts. cordon+drain in progress.

tess: note: rolling restarts will cause short latency spikes, will post a customer advisory in #support.

customer-ops: posted customer advisory to impacted accounts (msg id: sup-3942). will update customers after 30m monitoring window.

ajay: heap dumps uploaded to S3 at s3://redwood-dumps/7169876543/*. Grep shows pattern repeated across hosts. attaching small excerpt: `kv_slab: used=18432 free_chunks=128 frag_ratio=0.73`.

simon: temp mitigation ideas: 1) reduce slab size granularity to encourage coalescing; 2) force compaction after request runloop; 3) more aggressive eviction of long-tail prefixes. Implementing (1) & (2) as quick toggles.

maria: summary of actions applied: canary pinned to low-footprint model, increased kv compaction frequency, raised eviction cadence, cordoned two flaky nodes and draining. monitoring for error-rate and memory growth.

tess: :thumbsup: I'll watch the customer channel and post updates.

incident-bot: Status check scheduled in 10m. Please update thread with any new findings or customer escalations.

maria: immediate ask to eng-runtime if error rate not back to baseline by +30m we escalate. tagging @simon @ajay for follow-up investigation on slab defragger design.
